title: Walk 17: put a project on a host and take it off again

steps.say: Start the two mock daemons and the interface with the host stand-ins as described in the guided walk. Create the walk folder and invented keys first: mkdir -p /tmp/porelo-walk/keys /tmp/porelo-walk/tresor && ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -C walk-invented -f /tmp/porelo-walk/keys/walk_ed25519. Use only invented answers in this walk.
Open Projects in the rail, choose checkout, then its menu and Put this project on a server…. The title names the project and the first step is Where it is rented.

Give the Scaleway project id walk and keep account porelo. Read where the id is found in the Scaleway console and which saved provider key is used. Next stays unavailable until the step is complete. Click Next.

The drive is Tresorit. Choose /tmp/porelo-walk/tresor as Its synced folder on this computer. Its path appears beside Choose…, and The tresor's name in Tresorit fills with tresor. Change that name to walk; the server syncs by this name, while the folder holds this computer's copy. The signing-key field appears; the verified project bundle will be written into porelo-host in this folder.

Give signing key /tmp/porelo-walk/keys/walk_ed25519.pub. Each path field has Choose… beside it. Click Back and check the project id and account stayed; click Next to return and check the drive answers stayed. Then click Next to Your ssh keys.

The private ssh key comes first. Type /tmp/porelo-walk/keys/walk_ed25519.pub there: it is refused as a public key, and Next cannot run. Try ~nobody/key: only ~/ is understood, so it is also refused before any host starts. Give /tmp/porelo-walk/keys/walk_ed25519 as the private key and /tmp/porelo-walk/keys/walk_ed25519.pub as the public one. Each has its own Choose…. Click Next.

In A test collection, choose /tmp/porelo-walk/porelo-host and enter the digest printed by sha256sum /tmp/porelo-walk/porelo-host. Click Next. Check and start opens with A server for the project checkout and shows the values from every step. Nothing has been rented yet.

Read every answer, then click Put it on a server. Check that the tresor folder holds porelo-host/checkout.bundle. The wizard closes and Machines shows checkout server as In preparation. It shows the current step in its own words and about the time left in all and in that step. A stop says Needs you; the server is not a ready machine yet.

Click the In preparation row to open its protocol. All steps and standard error stay available here while setup runs. Close it; the run stays under Machines. A refusal keeps this row, its fix and its protocol instead of showing a ready machine.

Open Needs you in the rail. Its host setup row says on checkout server and names what the host needs. Click Complete setup on the host to open the protocol and its stop. Enter an invented plain Tresorit e-mail address. There must be no password, code or passphrase field.

Click Open a terminal on the host. Read the warning about the visible one-time code. Type an invented password, then an invented one-time code, then a vault passphrase twice into the terminal prompts. Each command says what completed and what comes next.
When the host terminal ends, click Done. Setup resumes without answers, then opens a terminal on this computer to finish the VPN. Machines stays at Setting up the VPN.

Type your sudo password into this computer’s VPN terminal. It checks the endpoint, pings the server and waits for a fresh handshake. Only then the VPN terminal and setup dialog close themselves, and no private temporary configuration stays in the runtime directory.

Open Machines. checkout server now appears as a ready machine only after the VPN check. In the server menu, Save the VPN connection… is for another device; Bring the VPN up repeats the same checked root step on this computer.

Open Full protocol to read every step and the words on standard error, including the earlier stop. Close the protocol and open Machines, then checkout server. It should answer through the second mock daemon, with only checkout and no work run yet.

Return to Machines and open checkout server's ⋯ menu. Bring the VPN up and Take the VPN down are offered here and on its page. Choose Bring the VPN up. A terminal on this computer shows sudo install -m 600 with the saved path as one argument, then sudo wg-quick up porelo. The line above says it needs root and sudo asks here. Stop at this terminal: type nothing under sudo.

Cancel the still-running VPN command and confirm Cancel it; if it has already ended, click Done. No saved file is deleted without asking. Open checkout server from the rail, then Projects and its checkout project. Press Messages and the project’s room on the project page. Before joining, the transport says on the server and gives no server-only address. Read the name rule under the field; type Michi and check that the field itself reads michi. Try Join; a refused join or failed forward must say why here and must not show a joined login. Change the name and check that the refusal clears. If joining and forwarding succeed, follow the numbered steps: Open Element opens https://app.element.io/ without a login in the address. Choose Sign in, Edit the homeserver, paste the Homeserver URL, sign in with the Matrix ID and Password, then join the Room by its name. Read the line explaining that a task mention is a pill picked from the client’s list. Close Messages to continue.

Open Projects in the rail, choose checkout on the host, then its menu and Put this project on a server…. Check that the last project id and account are already filled in Where it is rented, then Next.

Check that the tresor, signing key and local folder are restored. Next opens Your ssh keys with both paths filled. Click Next and check the test collection and its SHA-256 are restored too, then Next to Check and start. All restored answers remain editable.

The project dialog still offers Take it off the server. To try the Machines route, leave the wizard and open Machines, then checkout server. Its page and menu offer Take this server down. Return to Machines, open checkout server’s ⋯ menu, and choose Remove from this list.

The warning says the server keeps running and billing, explains adding it back by its tag, and offers Take this server down beside removal. Cancel to keep it listed. Open its ⋯ menu again and choose Take this server down.
Read the confirmation naming the project tasks, room and files that end. No field needs typing again. Click Take this server down; the host reports its give-back step and finishes with Done.

Close the teardown dialog and check Machines: checkout server has been removed; the first mock machine remains. Record anything that differed. To try a refusal or a slow step, change the situation in host-standin.json and reopen the dialog.
